input.rationale: The parent finding was established with default configuration flags. This successor runs the witness scenario under the recommended production configuration, PreVote and CheckQuorum, and with the logical clock running while the invocation is outstanding, so the held proposal cannot be attributed to default flags or to a clock that never advances. A control under the same flags shows the cluster still accepts and commits proposals from a member that was never removed.

scope.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API with Config.PreVote and Config.CheckQuorum both true. Node 1 campaigns and becomes leader at term 1 in configuration {1,2,3}; a remove-3 ConfChange is proposed on the leader and applied on every node; node 3 is then re-added by a committed ConfChange with leader 1 unchanged; the logical clock is advanced ten rounds with delivery between rounds; then Node.Propose is invoked on the re-added node 3 with a 1200 ms context and a 900 ms observation window, followed by a control invocation on never-removed node 2. Events record returned values, errors, elapsed times, membership, leader and payload presence.
assumptions: Reliable per-sender ordered in-process delivery.
Ticks are delivered in ten rounds with delivery between rounds so heartbeats keep the followers' election timers reset while both timeouts advance.
CheckQuorum's activity tracking is therefore exercised (the leader keeps quorum) and PreVote's pre-election phase is available, but no election is triggered during the observation.
excluded: Message loss, partitions and leader changes
RawNode paths and async storage writes
Joint-consensus removal forms (covered separately)

experiment.prefix: Start nodes 1,2,3 with a MemoryStorage per node whose ConfState voters are {1,2,3} and with PreVote and CheckQuorum enabled. Node 1 campaigns at term 1 and becomes leader; every node reports leader 1 and node 1 has applied the initial entry. Propose a remove-3 ConfChange on node 1 and wait until node 3's own configuration excludes it; propose an add-3 ConfChange and wait until node 3 is a voter again with leader still 1. Advance the clock ten rounds with delivery between rounds and record the resulting context (leader, leader state, membership). Invoke Node.Propose on node 3 with a 1200 ms context, observe for 900 ms, and record the result and whether its payload is committed anywhere. Then invoke Node.Propose on node 2 and record its result and committed payload.
experiment.responsibility: Client-facing obligation of the Node interface under the recommended configuration: a proposal from a re-added voter with a healthy known leader must reach a decision or return an error rather than staying pending, while proposals from other members must continue to complete.

comparisons.description: Under PreVote and CheckQuorum with the clock running, the re-added voter's invocation did not return inside the window.
Its payload was not committed anywhere.
Control: the never-removed member's invocation under the same flags returned.
Control: its payload was committed on all nodes, so the group was healthy under those flags.

scope.description: Exploration with no fixed requirement: three real raft state machines (ids 1,2,3, ElectionTick 10, HeartbeatTick 1, in-memory storage whose ConfState is {1,2,3}) driven for 300 steps per seed, with random connectivity masks that change the reachable peers, per-message drop decisions, random ticks, random proposals from members, random campaigns and random leader transfer requests. Committed entries are applied through the captured log interface, and safety monitors run after every step: one leader per term, applied entries immutable per node and index, identical entry for the same index across nodes, committed index monotonic per node, and every previously applied entry present in the log of a state machine that reports itself leader. Events report any violation with seed, invariant and detail, and one summary per seed with the exercised counts.
assumptions: Messages are delivered in random batches of up to three per step and may be dropped, which models lossy, reordering-prone transport without permanent partitions.
The confinement masks change independently per node, so asymmetric partitions occur.
Entries are persisted to the in-memory storage through the captured helpers before messages are delivered, matching the documented usage.
No configuration changes are injected in this exploration; membership transitions are covered by the deterministic experiments.
excluded: Membership changes, snapshot transfer and restart recovery (covered by deterministic experiments or left for later)
Crash-stop faults: state machines keep running for the whole scenario
Any claim of absence of defects beyond the two explored seeds and 300 steps each

scope.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API in one process. Node 1 campaigns and becomes leader at term 1 in the configuration {1,2,3}; a ConfChangeV2 with Transition JointExplicit and a single remove change for node 3 is proposed on node 1, which enters a joint configuration that is never left. The joint state is not left because the proposal uses the explicit transition and the harness never proposes the empty leave change.

excluded: Removal from both halves (covered by the witness scenario in the parent investigation)

scope.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API in one process, with per-node MemoryStorage kept up to date by the driver (HardState and appended entries). Node 1 is elected, a payload is committed on all three nodes, node 2 is stopped, a second payload is committed while it is down, node 2 is restarted from its storage by rebuilding a raft instance on the same storage, the logical clock is advanced in ten rounds with delivery between rounds, and then the harness records the restarted node's leader, its applied entries, the recovered payload's presence on every node, and a subsequent proposal from node 2.
assumptions: The storage directory equivalent is the same MemoryStorage instance, so the restart sees exactly what the driver persisted: HardState on every Ready and all appended entries.
No snapshot is taken, so the restarted member catches up through the ordinary append path rather than by installing a snapshot.
The clock is advanced after the restart because a restarted member otherwise has no traffic from the leader with which to learn it; this is a property of the harness, not of the target.
Membership is unchanged in this scenario, so the storage's ConfState stays valid across the restart.
excluded: Snapshot installation and storage loss at the restarted member
Multiple simultaneous restarts and crash-stop during the restart
Message loss, ticks during the outage, and membership changes

result.summary: Submitting the robustness variant of the primary scenario under the recommended production configuration, so the held proposal cannot be attributed to default flags or to a clock that never advances. It is a successor of the ticks experiment in the primary investigation: PreVote and CheckQuorum are both enabled, the logical clock is advanced ten rounds with delivery between rounds before the invocation, and the witness and control events carry their own names. Four comparisons cover the re-added voter's invocation staying pending, its payload not being committed, and the never-removed member's invocation returning and committing under the same flags. A local dry run through the framework's own comparator shows all four as complete holds: the witness invocation returned false at 901 ms with leader 1 still in StateLeader and the member a voter, its payload absent, while the control returned true and committed on all three nodes. The submission is validated with execution requested, and its receipt will be interpreted next, replacing the last implicit gap in the parent account about configuration flags.

scope.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API in one process. scope.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API in one process, with per-node MemoryStorage kept up to date by the driver (HardState and appended entries). Node 1 is elected, a payload is committed on all three nodes, node 2 is stopped, a second payload is committed while it is down, node 2 is restarted from its storage by rebuilding a raft instance on the same storage, the logical clock is advanced in ten rounds with delivery between rounds, and then the harness records the restarted node's leader, its applied entries, the recovered payload's presence on every node, and a subsequent proposal from node 2.

Membership is unchanged in this scenario, so the storage's ConfState stays valid across the restart.
excluded: Snapshot installation and storage loss at the restarted member
